name: State Socialism
summary: State socialism holds that socialism is achieved and run through the state: public ownership of the means of production, usually coordinated by a central economic plan, in place of private ownership and market allocation. Its strands differ on how the state is won (Lassalle's universal suffrage, Bolshevik revolution) and on how democratic it is, but share the view that the state is an instrument of social transformation rather than something to abolish at once.
scope: The statist core of socialism as realized in Soviet-type systems (Lenin's 1918 programme, Stalin's economic writings, the 1936 Soviet Constitution), with Ferdinand Lassalle's view of the state as its precursor. Anarchist, libertarian-socialist, market-socialist and council-communist critics, and Bismarck's social-insurance 'state socialism', are excluded. Where the Lassallean and democratic strands differ from Soviet-type ones (party monopoly, revolution, class view of the state) the answer is marked split or low confidence.

keyFigures.name: Vladimir Lenin
keyFigures.role: Leader of the Bolshevik state that built the first state-owned, planned economy

keyFigures.name: Joseph Stalin
keyFigures.role: Codified socialism in one country and the Soviet planned economy

sources.title: State socialism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Definition, strands (Lassallean, Marxist-Leninist, Bismarckian, Fabian), state ownership, planning, party role, critics' state-capitalism charge

sources.title: The Workingmen's Programme
sources.author: Ferdinand Lassalle (1862)
sources.usedFor: The state as educator of humanity toward freedom, rejection of the night-watchman state, universal suffrage, legitimate property

sources.title: The Immediate Tasks of the Soviet Government
sources.author: V. I. Lenin (1918)
sources.usedFor: Accounting and control, bank nationalisation, one-man management, labour discipline, piece-work, state monopolies and foreign trade, dictatorship against exploiters

sources.author: J. V. Stalin (1952)
sources.usedFor: Commodity circulation versus planning, collective-farm property, preconditions of communism, from each according to needs

sources.title: Constitution (Fundamental Law) of the USSR, 1936
sources.author: Soviet Union
sources.usedFor: State and cooperative property, planning, party as leading core, rights and duties, church-state separation, equality of races, recall, elections

universal-healthcare.rationale: The 1936 Constitution guarantees material support in sickness, and a state that owns the economy treats health care as a public service.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wages are set centrally under planning and raising low pay fits the aim, but a statutory minimum wage is a market-economy device so this is inferred.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Stalin held that commodity circulation increasingly hampers planning and should give way to centrally controlled product exchange.

public-ownership.rationale: State ownership of the means of production is the defining feature of state socialism, far beyond energy, rail and utilities.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Where the state owns industry, taxation is secondary, but reducing private wealth is the aim and Lenin wanted compulsory duties to fall first on the rich; inferred.

unions-good.rationale: Unions are described as channels of worker participation, though in Soviet-type states they work under party and plan direction.

property-fundamental.rationale: The Constitution makes state and cooperative property the basis of the system and confines private holdings to personal items and small labour-based plots.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Adherents would nationalize large corporations rather than regulate them, so agreement is only loose and inferred.

cut-welfare.rationale: Social insurance, free education and security in old age and sickness are written into the constitutional order as guaranteed rights.

worker-ownership.rationale: Ownership is vested in the state on behalf of the whole people, not in each firm's workforce, which critics note leaves workers without real control.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Lenin's stress on iron discipline and state coercion against exploiters implies a security-first attitude; inferred.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from the disciplined, work-as-duty ethos of the model.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Article 123 makes promoting racial or national hatred punishable by law.

strong-leader.rationale: Lenin backed dictatorial powers for individual executives and strong central direction, though not as a rejection of party structures.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the state's monopoly on armed force.

empower-police-military.rationale: Inferred from Lenin's insistence on coercion against the exploiters and a strong state during the transition.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the state's moral-labour framing and women's equality guarantees.

decide-locally.rationale: Central planning and a unified state economic plan mean strategic decisions are taken at national level.

rehabilitation.rationale: Lenin favoured courts to enforce labour discipline and re-education of the idle; inferred.

traditional-family.rationale: Not defined by the ideology; Soviet-type states shifted between family support and its relaxation.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed; historical Soviet-type states did not recognize it, though modern parties differ.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from women's equality guarantees and Soviet-type practice.

more-religion-public.rationale: Article 124 separates church from state and school from church while permitting anti-religious propaganda.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The Constitution guarantees equal rights regardless of race or nationality; active redress is inferred.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The sources address legal equality of women, not a theory of gender.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Not a core concern; the ideology stresses class and cultural advancement rather than national tradition.

gradual-change.rationale: Strands split: Lassalle and Fabian variants are gradualist, Bolshevik ones revolutionary.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Not addressed; socialism in one country implies priority for the state, while internationalism pulls the other way.

free-trade.rationale: Lenin supported a state monopoly on foreign trade to shield the socialist economy from foreign capital.

nation-first.rationale: Socialism in one country puts the socialist state first, but the ideology also claims internationalism.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from hostility to great-power intervention.

open-borders.rationale: Not addressed; Soviet-type states controlled movement; inferred.

limit-growth.rationale: Stalin made continuous expansion of production, with the means of production growing fastest, a precondition of communism.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not addressed; a state able to plan could act but growth priority pulls the other way.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The doctrine ties progress to developing productive forces, though not as a claim that technology solves everything.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Lenin stressed a material base in fuel and heavy industry; nuclear power is inferred as state-led energy.

revolution-justified.rationale: Bolshevik and Soviet-type states arose from revolution and Lenin defends coercion against the exploiters, though Lassallean variants use the ballot.

experts-over-public.rationale: Lenin paid high salaries to bourgeois specialists and wanted planning by trained managers; inferred as a general stance.

central-planning.rationale: Stalin and the Soviet model rest on a state economic plan directing production and distribution.

socialized-markets.rationale: State socialists see commodity circulation as a brake on planning, not an acceptable permanent mechanism.

land-value-tax.rationale: Land and means of production would be owned by the state rather than taxed.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from limits on private accumulation.

basic-income.rationale: Work is a duty and pay follows work, so unconditional income contradicts the principle.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Lenin's state foreign-trade monopoly is a stronger form of protecting domestic industry.

state-directs-investment.rationale: State direction of investment through the plan is central to Soviet-type economies.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The model replaces both corporate and small private ownership with state and cooperative property.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Stalin saw commodity circulation giving way to product exchange on the road to communism, though wages remain during the socialist stage.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Lenin wanted the banks nationalized as centres of public accounting, not abolished or left to the market.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Unions and enterprises operate inside the plan, not as autonomous state-recognized bargaining partners.

one-party-rule.rationale: Article 126 makes the Communist Party the leading core of all organizations, though democratic variants dissent.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The model is a republic of soviets with elective bodies and no hereditary privilege.

democracy-best.rationale: Lenin called Soviets a higher democracy but argued dictatorship against exploiters is necessary.

direct-votes.rationale: Representative soviets, not referendums, are the constitutional form.

workers-councils.rationale: Lenin presented Soviets as the basis of power with recall, though in practice under party leadership.

right-to-secede.rationale: Soviet constitutions granted it formally, but the practice and stance of adherents were restrictive.

natural-rulers.rationale: Rule is justified by class and party leadership, not natural aptitude, but the vanguard idea sits close.

political-violence-never.rationale: Lenin argues coercion and dictatorship are necessary because exploiters will resist.

war-builds-character.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the emphasis on peaceful construction.

separate-church-state.rationale: Article 124 of the 1936 Soviet Constitution states that the church is separated from the state and the school from the church, to ensure freedom of conscience.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Law rests on the Constitution and the state plan, with religion separated from the state.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Courts and defence are state functions under state socialism.

military-superiority.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine that a socialist state must stay strong amid hostile states.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The Constitution guarantees equal rights regardless of nationality and race.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Lenin's account of exploiters resisting the transition rests on class struggle as the motor of history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Pay follows work during socialism and Lenin accepted unequal pay as a temporary tribute; equality of needs awaits communism.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: None of the opened sources address indigenous land rights; the answer is split because land is state property but nationalities have equal rights.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Inferred from anti-imperialism; not documented in the opened sources.

civilizational-union.rationale: Class, not civilization, is the unit of solidarity.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Work is a civic duty and point of honour, not a vehicle for self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Rights are guaranteed in conformity with the interests of working people and work is a duty.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The sources treat nature as a base for production and say nothing on its intrinsic value, so adherents have no settled view.

limit-population.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from an expansion-oriented outlook.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Stalin's path to communism runs through expanded industrial production and shorter working days.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Inferred from the priority on developing productive forces.

human-enhancement.rationale: Neither Lassalle, Lenin nor Stalin address bodily enhancement; Stalin's polytechnical education is the nearest topic and is not about enhancement.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Not addressed; planning by accounting and control is relevant but unspecified.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Inferred from emphasis on comprehensive state accounting and control.

restore-past-order.rationale: The doctrine aims at transformation to socialism and treats restoring the former order as counter-revolution.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Policy is guided by doctrine, though Lenin was pragmatic about temporary concessions.

direct-action.rationale: Change is directed by party and state, not leaderless direct action.

means-match-ends.rationale: Lenin justified coercion and dictatorship as means distinct from the classless end.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Stalin's communism rests on higher productivity and culture.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Stalin looked to polytechnical education so no one is tied to one occupation, a gradual aim.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Stalin names from each according to ability, to each according to needs as the later stage after socialism.

production-for-use.rationale: Nationalisation is meant to turn profit to public finance and later production for use.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Lenin's treatment of exploiters and expropriation takes profit as unearned; Lassallean strands differ.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Lenin argues dictatorship in the transition is necessary against resisting exploiters.

collective-farming.rationale: Stalin wants collective-farm property raised toward public property and collective farming expanded.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Marxist-Leninist strands hold this; not directly sourced in the opened texts.

taxation-theft.rationale: Lassalle mocked the night-watchman state as a policeman's idea and made the state an agent of collective purpose.

harm-principle.rationale: Freedoms are guaranteed only in conformity with the interests of working people.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Rights are tied to class and social duties.

conscription.rationale: Inferred from the defence duty of citizens in the socialist state.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Not addressed; Soviet-type states restricted exit.

state-as-business.rationale: Lassalle sees the state as the educator of humanity, not a business serving customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: Lassalle's state enables collective achievement beyond individual means, and the Constitution guarantees work and leisure.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation runs through soviets and party-led public organizations, not corporate bodies.

total-state.rationale: Lassalle gives the state educational purposes and planning covers the economy, but not all life.

national-rebirth.rationale: Rooted in class transformation, not national decadence.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Not a stated aim; Lenin and Stalin concentrate on building socialism inside the state, which weakly counts against expansion.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority rests on elective soviets and law, not personal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: The Constitution guarantees rights to work and equality, abolishing serf-type status.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Marxist ideology critique implies it, yet scientific socialism claims objective truth.

universal-morality.rationale: Morality is class-conditioned in the doctrine; inferred.

single-common-good.rationale: Lassalle's state serves the progress of humanity as a whole; inferred.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The sources are silent on Zionism; Soviet policy shifted over time, so no stable adherent position can be inferred.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The opened sources do not mention diaspora return; the question lies outside the ideology's core.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is not addressed in the sources; Soviet language policy varied by period.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Lenin favoured one-man management in enterprises over workers' votes.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Planned economies do not fit this debate; not addressed.

economic-freedom.rationale: The doctrine curtails market freedom to enable planning and denies the dependency.

rule-by-example.rationale: Lenin insists on law, courts and compulsion.

national-self-determination.rationale: Equal rights of nations are constitutional; the exact doctrine is inferred.

force-without-un.rationale: The ideology predates the UN Security Council debate and the sources say nothing on force abroad, so it is left neutral.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Anti-religious propaganda and scientific outlook; inferred.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The 1936 Constitution ties support to citizens, but immigrants' entitlements are not discussed, so adherents are unspecified.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Work is a civic duty for able-bodied citizens, and support follows labour.

class-collaboration.rationale: Lenin treats exploiters as resisting classes to be suppressed.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Inferred; Soviet policy generally preserved museums as public property.

dominated-front.rationale: Third-world fronts against Western powers are not in the opened sources; Soviet bloc policy suggests sympathy but this is not stated.

workers-nation.rationale: Class internationalism sits against national organizing, though socialism in one country complicates it.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The Constitution declares women equal in all spheres.

ban-interest.rationale: State banking makes private interest moot; not addressed.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Article 123 of the 1936 Constitution makes equal rights regardless of race an indefeasible law and makes any restriction of rights or advocacy of racial exclusiveness punishable.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Lassalle saw the state as an independent instrument of justice while Marxist-Leninists call it a class tool.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Lenin stressed fuel and iron as the material base for industry; inferred.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Immigration and assimilation are not discussed in the sources; Soviet policy stressed equal nationalities but also a common socialist culture.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiracy claim foreign to the ideology.

proportional-representation.rationale: The Constitution specifies equal direct elections of soviets by constituency; PR is outside the sources.

national-mission.rationale: Socialism in one country versus export of revolution.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Sources stress legal equality, not structural analysis.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Critics allege elite formation but adherents defend the party's role.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not addressed; the equal-rights guarantees of the Constitution make adherents lean against coercive eugenics, but without evidence.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The sources do not treat accountability for past security-force killings; adherents defended their states' security organs but this is not documented here.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Lassalle called the night-watchman idea a policeman's idea.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Stalin's doctrine of socialism in one country holds socialism can be built in a single state.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Not discussed in the opened sources; Marxist anti-colonialism points toward yes but the source base does not state it.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Equal rights regardless of nationality; inferred.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Freedom of worship is guaranteed; not addressed further.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Article 124 separates schools from the church.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Lassalle rejected withering away and Stalin legitimised a strong state under hostile encirclement.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Soviet claims of popular rule coexist with party leadership.

trade-surplus.rationale: Lenin's state trade monopoly manages trade to serve the plan rather than to maximize exports, so the question is not addressed.

population-transfer.rationale: Not addressed; deportations were practice but not doctrine.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Lenin accepts coercion and dictatorship over exploiters.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Lenin wants planned cooperation, accounting and discipline instead.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Nominations are reserved to public organizations and the party leads all of them.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: This republican concept does not appear in the sources; the ideology's liberty talk is about class and material guarantees.

separated-powers.rationale: Soviets combined legislative and executive power.

vanguard-party.rationale: Article 126 calls the party the vanguard of working people.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Social guarantees and class orientation favour the working poor.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: State housing is public property; personal ownership of a home is permitted, so inferred.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Lenin demands iron labour discipline and punishment of violations.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Poverty is blamed on exploitation, not population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The Constitution commits to equality of nationalities.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Lenin accepts dictatorship against internal exploiters.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Planned pricing is part of the model.

party-controls-media.rationale: Press freedom is bounded by working-class interest with party leadership.

party-commands-army.rationale: Party is leading core of all state organizations; inferred.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalization rules are not discussed in the sources, and the Constitution says nothing on waiting periods.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Lenin cites the Paris Commune principle but concedes exceptions.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Lenin demands iron discipline and obedience after debate.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Inferred from stress on state control.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Collective soviet bodies were the form.

clerical-rule.rationale: Article 124 of the 1936 Constitution separates the church from the state and recognises freedom of anti-religious propaganda, leaving clergy no political authority.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Not addressed in the opened sources; Soviet practice defended the state.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Soviet censorship served ideology, not specifically virtue.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The Constitution sets no term limits; inferred.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Housing is largely state-owned and allocated, so tenancy remains.

people-in-arms.rationale: Not documented; state armies were standing.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Stalin aimed to end town-country differences, not exalt rural life.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Reunification of divided nations is not addressed; Soviet-type states split on it by period and bloc interest.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Equal rights for women and universal education; inferred.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Anti-religious propaganda is protected and schools are separated from churches.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Citizenship tied to territory and class equality; inferred.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine that political change needs economic transformation.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Bolsheviks dissolved it but Lassallean strands use suffrage.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Aid duties are not discussed in the sources; Lenin's anti-imperialism points one way, the socialism-in-one-country doctrine the other.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Lenin wanted banks nationalized under state control.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial concessions are not addressed in the opened sources.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Personal property is protected but subordinate to socialist property.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Adherents hold the Soviet economy was socialist; state-capitalist is the critics' label.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk is not discussed; planning could support it but the growth priority in Stalin's text pulls the other way.

collective-defense.rationale: Inferred from encirclement doctrine and bloc alliances.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Soviet practice did not follow a single doctrine on annexation consent.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Separation of church and state with state curbs on church influence.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Party is leading core of all organizations.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Constitution grants formal rights while practice differed.

character-from-environment.rationale: Stalin stresses education and cultural advancement shaping people.

space-expansion.rationale: Space is not addressed by the opened texts; Soviet practice supported it as a prestige project, which is not doctrine.

leader-cult.rationale: Practiced under Stalin and condemned later.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family-law presumptions are outside the sources, which address only equal rights for women.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Soviet orthodoxy holds socialism built; critics claim otherwise.

land-redistribution.rationale: Initial land decrees gave land to peasants but the model collectivized it.

refugee-return.rationale: Refugee return rights are not covered by the sources.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Freedom of worship and anti-religious propaganda are guaranteed.

women-must-cover.rationale: Article 122 of the 1936 Constitution grants women equal rights with men in all spheres of life, which runs against compulsory covering, though dress codes are not mentioned.

common-currency.rationale: Currency unions are not addressed; Lenin's emphasis on state banks and accounting says nothing on shared currencies.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Class, not kinship, is the unit.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The Constitution grants equal rights to nationalities but the sources do not set out national-cultural autonomy as such.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Stalin refers to adjusting relations of production to productive forces.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Not addressed; the Soviet model places the legislature and party above courts but the sources do not frame the liberal-democratic debate.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Equal rights without quotas in the opened text.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Foreign trade monopoly and socialism in one country imply autarkic tendencies.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Trade agreements with binding standards are not discussed; Lenin's foreign-trade monopoly makes the question moot.

moral-incentives.rationale: Lenin backed piece-work and wage differentials; Stalin kept pay by work.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Vanguard party model, not foco; inferred.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Equal rights regardless of origin; no hereditary privilege.

history-own-civilization.rationale: School history curricula are not addressed; Soviet education stressed class and socialism rather than civilization.

patriotic-education.rationale: Socialism in one country drives loyalty to socialist state; inferred.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Not addressed; the Constitution bars racial privilege but does not discuss admissions preferences.

public-money-creation.rationale: Lenin nationalised banks as centres of accounting.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Marxist crisis theory; not directly sourced.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Cultivating influence in former imperial lands is not covered; Soviet practice is contested.

delink-world-market.rationale: Lenin's state foreign-trade monopoly and Stalin's socialism in one country partly resemble delinking, but dependency theory is not in the sources.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: The theory is a Leninist concept not found in the opened sources, so no position is documented.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Article 123 of the 1936 Constitution makes any direct or indirect restriction of a citizen's rights on grounds of race or nationality punishable by law, in economic as well as public life.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Rights are conditioned by working-class interest.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Treaty voidance is not discussed in the opened sources.

elective-rulers.rationale: Soviets are elected by universal vote.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The Constitution allows recall of deputies but the right to resist a ruler is not stated, and strands differ.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Supreme Soviet as supreme organ; inferred.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal welfare is not addressed by any of the opened sources.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use is not addressed; no position can be derived from the opened sources.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Obligation falls on state, not privileged class.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: This is a Western Marxist thesis; state socialists use mass culture for education so the sources give no position.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian cultural hegemony is not in the opened sources; Lenin stresses coercion more than consent.

native-born-offices.rationale: The Constitution gives equal rights to all citizens regardless of nationality, which weighs against reserving offices for the native born.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Revanchist claims are not discussed; the sources treat the socialist state, not irredentism.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The Constitution's equality of nationalities and races argues against ranking descendants of settlers and natives.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The 1936 text predates postwar antifascist constitutions; the stance is inferred from Soviet self-image, not stated.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not addressed in the opened sources; Marxist historical materialism points toward economic causes including slavery.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Monuments are not addressed in the sources, and Soviet states removed old regime symbols.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: The Constitution asserts equal rights for women, but programmes for male disadvantage are not discussed.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; the 1936 text only addresses women's equality in law.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The Constitution makes the party the leading core over state bodies, so a separate guardian role for the army conflicts with it.

paid-care-work.rationale: The sources do not discuss wages for domestic labour; socialist states socialized some care via public services.

state-harmful.rationale: Lassalle called the state the training of humanity toward freedom and rejected its withering away, so the state is the instrument of socialism.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred: the 1936 Constitution stresses duties and family support, but state socialism has no distinct doctrine on filial duty.

office-by-exam.rationale: Inferred: officials are elected and the party leads under the 1936 Constitution, with no examination system.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Lenin defends state monopolies including foreign trade to protect the socialist economy from foreign capital.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred: state socialism has no stated position, and its strands differ.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Inferred: the 1936 Constitution provides for recall of deputies, though the Lassallean strand did not.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Old-age maintenance is a state social-insurance matter, not private savings accounts.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land is state property or held by collective farms in perpetual use, which fits holding it by use rather than outright ownership.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred: the Supreme Soviet formally approved the budget, though the party directed the plan.

single-official-language.rationale: Inferred from the Constitution's equality of nations and races, which does not impose a single state language.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from state ownership of land and national control of the economy.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred: the Constitution guarantees equality of races, and the doctrine treats inequality as class based rather than judging outcomes.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred: Stalin wants growing consumption of the people but the sources do not address consumerism as a harm.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Not addressed; the Soviet-type and Lassallean strands differ.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Not addressed; the Soviet-type and Lassallean strands differ.

corporate-influence.rationale: State socialists see private ownership of capital as giving the owners power over politics, which is a reason to bring it under public ownership.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred: a state running the economy and foreign trade monopolies (Lenin 1918) would control foreign funding, but the doctrine does not address it.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred: Soviet-type states supported mothers and families through state allowances, but it is not a doctrinal point.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred: with public ownership of land the question barely arises and adherents have no settled view.

job-guarantee.rationale: The 1936 Constitution guarantees the right to work, and the plan allocates jobs.

democratic-peace.rationale: Inferred: Lassallean and democratic strands could accept it, while the Marxist-Leninist strand rejects it, so adherents are split.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Inferred: state socialism sees the state as the instrument of social transformation and expects obedience to its law.

non-intervention.rationale: Inferred: the Lassallean strand is silent on it and the Soviet strand mixed non-interference with internationalist support for revolutions.

industrial-unions.rationale: Inferred: Soviet-type state socialism organised unions by industry within the planned economy.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The 1936 Constitution makes equality of races and nationalities a principle and penalises racial hostility.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred: the Soviet-type state upheld legal marriage and state protection of the family, and Lassalle saw the state as the guarantor of social institutions.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred: state-planned economies run by one party kept information under central control.

local-production.rationale: Inferred: central planning aims at national coordination of production, not local self-sufficiency.

informal-organisation.rationale: State socialism relies on the disciplined party and state apparatus, and rejects loose small-group organisation as inadequate to run an economy.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Inferred: the state as the instrument of transformation and monopoly over foreign trade imply national law taking precedence over supranational authority.

religious-nation.rationale: The 1936 Constitution separates church from state and the strand is secular; the community is defined by class and citizenship.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a doctrine of sovereign, equal states building socialism and from the 1936 constitution's equality of peoples.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The 1936 constitution makes the economy a single planned whole with national property, leaving no room for regions to keep their own revenue.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The 1936 constitution protects citizens' personal property while socialist property in the means of production is the economic base.

defeat-communism.rationale: State socialism is a form of communism or socialism and so seeks its extension, not its defeat.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: State ownership and delivery of services is the core of the model, as in Lenin's programme for state organisation of the economy.

religion-illusion.rationale: Not a defining issue for the statist core; inferred from the secular socialist tradition from Lassalle to the Soviet state.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist inheritance that capitalism built the productive base for socialism.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The 1936 constitution guarantees women equal rights in economic life, implying economic reorganisation as the route; inferred.

socialized-care.rationale: The 1936 constitution provides for state protection of mothers and children through institutions; inferred for housework.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Not addressed; the 1936 constitution guarantees instruction in native languages rather than linguistic purging.

treaties-binding.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a statist view that the state acts for the public interest.

cooperative-communities.rationale: State socialism relies on the state and central plan, not on self-governing communes.

majority-settlement.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the 1936 constitution's equality of nations and races.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: State socialism sees itself as a socialist alternative to capitalism and does not look for a third course.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Inferred from the class-based, internationalist outlook of the strand, which does not rest claims on historical or religious ties.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not addressed; Soviet-type states were founded on anti-fascism and no strand of the doctrine denies fascist crimes.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred from Soviet-type practice, which criminalized homosexuality from 1934; the Lassallean strand is silent.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Lenin demands iron discipline and Soviet-type states barred opposition parties, though the Lassallean strand sought universal suffrage.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Inferred: Soviet-type states were atheist and restricted religion but did not enforce a religious order.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Inferred from the anti-imperialist and anti-capitalist stance of Lenin and the Soviet constitutions.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the secular outlook of the strand.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from secular rule in Soviet-type states.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Split: Lenin praised Soviet participation but also one-man management and central planning, and Lassalle sought state action from above.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Inferred: the strand treats class as primary and reads other oppressions through it.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the practice of Soviet-type states.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from state-directed medicine and conservative social practice.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Inferred: state socialism places itself on the left and in opposition to capitalism.

alienated-labor.rationale: Inferred from socialist critique of wage labour; Lassalle's Workingmen's Programme attacks the worker's condition under capital.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from class-based internationalism.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The 1936 Soviet Constitution places power in the working people, and the strand grounds the state in class and the people.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred from the separation of church and state in the 1936 Constitution.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from state protection of workers against employers.

social-market-economy.rationale: The strand replaces private ownership and market allocation with public ownership and planning, so a market economy tempered by regulation is not its aim.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The 1936 Constitution makes defence of the fatherland a sacred duty, and the strand sees the state as an instrument that needs force.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred from planned, public ownership meant to spread wealth, not let some grow rich first.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Inferred: Soviet-type states built a socialist bloc; Lassallean strand did not address it.

missingStatements.text: Foreign trade should be a state monopoly rather than conducted by private firms.
missingStatements.rationale: Lenin defends a state monopoly on foreign trade to protect the socialist economy from foreign capital, and it is a defining feature of the Soviet-type model.

missingStatements.text: Workers in publicly owned enterprises should submit to strict labour discipline and the authority of individual managers.
missingStatements.rationale: Lenin calls for iron discipline and one-man management, comparing it to an orchestra conductor, and supports courts punishing breaches.
missingStatements.declined: Specific to Leninist management practice; the stance is already covered by central-planning, workplace-democracy and one-party-rule, and adding it would burden every future audit.

notes: Strands diverge: Lassallean and democratic or Fabian state socialists accept parliamentary routes and reject one-party rule; Marxist-Leninists hold a party-led dictatorship of the proletariat. Critics (libertarian socialists, council communists, some Trotskyists) call Soviet-type systems state capitalism, which adherents reject.
